de.purpose: Dient der Darstellung der höchsten erreichten Diagnosesicherheit zu dem Diagnosezeitpunkt. Weiterhin dient der Archetyp der Darstellung der Diagnosesicherung durch die Beschreibung der Methoden und den Informationen, auf welchen die Krebsdiagnose basiert.
de.use:
Zur Darstellung der höchsten erreichten Diagnosesicherheit zu dem Diagnosezeitpunkt. Weiterhin dient der Archetype zur Darstellung der Diagnosesicherung durch die Beschreibung der Methoden und den Informationen, auf welchen die Krebsdiagnose basiert. Dieser Cluster Archetyp wurde speziell für den SLOT "Spezifische Angaben" des Archetyps EVALUATION.problem_diagnosis erstellt. 

Die mit diesem Archetyp dargestellte Information soll Kliniker dabei unterstützten, eine Krebsdiagnose besser beurteilen zu können. Dies ist besonders wichtig, wenn ein Kliniker Informationen über eine Krebsdiagnose eines Patienten erhält, die der Kliniker selber nicht diagnostiziert hat. Zum Beispiel, wenn ein Kliniker einen Patient eines anderen Arztes in einem Tumorboard begutachten soll.
de.misuse: Dieser Archetyp ist ausschließlich für die Darstellung der höchsten Diagnosesicherheit und der Diagnosesicherung von Krebsdiagnosen konzipiert worden und sollte nicht im Kontext von anderen Krankheiten verwendet werden.

nb.purpose: Brukes for å beskrive den høyest oppnådde graden av diagnostisk sikkerhet på diagnosetidspunktet. Videre brukes arketypen til å beskrive hvordan diagnosen er blitt bekreftet, gjennom dokumentasjon av metodene og informasjonen som ligger til grunn for kreftdiagnosen.
nb.use:
Brukes for å beskrive den høyeste oppnådde graden av diagnostisk sikkerhet på diagnosetidspunktet. I tillegg brukes denne arketypen til å dokumentere hvordan diagnosen ble bekreftet, gjennom beskrivelse av metodene og informasjonen som ligger til grunn for kreftdiagnosen. Denne CLUSTER‑arketypen er spesifikt utviklet for SLOT‑en “Spesifikke opplysninger” i arketypen EVALUATION.problem_diagnosis.

Informasjonen som representeres ved denne arketypen skal støtte klinikere i å vurdere en kreftdiagnose mer presist. Dette er særlig viktig når en kliniker mottar informasjon om en kreftdiagnose som vedkommende ikke selv har diagnostisert. For eksempel når en kliniker skal vurdere en pasient henvist fra en annen lege i et tverrfaglig klinikermøte (Multidisiplinært møte).
nb.misuse: Denne arketypen er utelukkende utviklet for å representere den høyeste graden av diagnostisk sikkerhet og bekreftelse av kreftdiagnoser, og skal ikke brukes i forbindelse med andre sykdommer.

en.purpose: To represent the highest level of diagnostic certainty achieved at the time of diagnosis. Furthermore, the archetype is used to describe how the diagnosis was confirmed, by documenting the methods and information on which the cancer diagnosis is based.
en.use:
Use to represent the highest level of diagnostic certainty achieved at the time of diagnosis. In addition, this archetype is used to document how the diagnosis was confirmed, by describing the methods and information on which the cancer diagnosis is based. This CLUSTER archetype has been specifically designed for the “Specific details” SLOT within the EVALUATION.problem_diagnosis archetype.

The information represented by this archetype is intended to support clinicians in assessing a cancer diagnosis more accurately. This is particularly important when a clinician receives information about a cancer diagnosis that they did not establish themselves—such as when evaluating a patient referred by another physician in a multidisciplinary tumour board.
en.misuse: This archetype has been designed exclusively to represent the highest level of diagnostic certainty and the diagnostic confirmation of cancer diagnoses, and should not be used in the context of other diseases.

at0000.description: Describes the highest level of diagnostic certainty recorded in the patient’s health record. It also documents which methods were used to establish the cancer diagnosis.

at0017.description: Documents the method, procedure, or information on which the diagnostic certainty is based.
at0017.comment: For example: clinical or imaging procedure.

at0094.description: The highest diagnostic certainty reached at the date of diagnosis.

at0095.description: The diagnosis was made solely by physical examination. No tumour‑specific diagnostics were performed.

at0096.description: The clinical diagnosis was made before the date of death. It may include several diagnostic techniques, such as X‑ray, endoscopy, other imaging methods, ultrasound, exploratory surgery (laparotomy, etc.) or autopsy. No microscopic tissue diagnosis exists.

at0097.description: Additional biochemical and/or immunological markers exist that are specific to a particular tumour site.

at0098.description: A cellular examination of material from the primary tumour site is available, including fluid aspirates collected via endoscopy or needle aspiration. Includes microscopic examination of peripheral blood smears and bone marrow aspirate smears.

at0099.description: A histological examination of tissue from a metastasis is available. This includes findings from autopsy.

at0100.description: A histological examination of tissue from the primary tumour is available. Includes all sectioning techniques and bone marrow biopsies, as well as samples of the primary tumour taken at autopsy.

at0101.description: Nothing is known regarding the level of diagnostic certainty.

at0102.description: The diagnostic certainty is based on a clinical identification of the tumour.

at0103.description: Neither a microscopic nor an imaging procedure was used for the diagnosis.

at0104.description: The tumour was identified during a surgical or endoscopic procedure. No microscopic confirmation exists.

at0105.description: The malignancy was reported by a physician in a medical record.

at0106.description: The tumour was identified through physical palpation.

at0107.description: The date and time at which the procedure was performed.

at0108.description: The malignancy was reported by a clinician using an imaging technique.

at0109.description: The malignancy was reported by a clinician using an imaging technique.

at0110.description: Tumour diagnosis by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

at0112.description: Tumour diagnosis by positron emission tomography (PET).

at0113.description: Tumour diagnosis by positron emission tomography combined with magnetic resonance imaging.

at0114.description: Tumour diagnosis by single‑photon emission computed tomography (SPECT).

at0115.description: Tumour diagnosis by another nuclear medicine imaging method not listed above (e.g., scintigraphy or gamma camera).

at0116.description: The date and time at which the procedure was performed.

at0117.description: Diagnostic certainty based on microscopic identification of the tumour.

at0118.description: Diagnostic certainty based on microscopic identification of the tumour.

at0119.description: Histological confirmation of the tumour diagnosis. Tissue has been examined microscopically.

at0122.description: The tumour diagnosis was confirmed by immunophenotyping.

at0123.description: The tumour diagnosis was microscopically confirmed, but the exact method is unknown.

at0124.description: The cancer diagnosis is based on a laboratory test or tumour marker analysis (e.g., alpha‑fetoprotein for liver cancer).

at0125.description: Diagnostic certainty is based on a procedure not covered by the previous items.

at0126.description: Diagnostic certainty is based on a procedure not covered by the previous items.

at0127.description: The date and time at which the procedure was performed.

at0128.description: The date and time at which the procedure was performed.

at0129.description: Additional information regarding the determination of diagnostic certainty.
at0129.comment: For example, notes about the quality of the diagnostic certainty may be recorded here.

at0131.description: The tumour diagnosis was confirmed by a genetic test.

at0132.description: Cytological confirmation of the tumour diagnosis. Cells were analysed in fluid samples. No tissue was examined microscopically.

at0133.description: Tumour diagnosis by positron emission tomography combined with computed tomography.
